text: Hi, how's it going? I'm a big coffee lover, so I guess I'll start there. I can't really start my day without a cup of coffee, and this morning was no different. I had one before I came to take this test, and I'm already looking forward to another one once it's over. I work in IT, and my days are pretty busy. I live in an apartment, and I'm pretty much a homebody. In my free time, I like listening to music, playing computer games, and reading. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell: coffee, music, and my computer. I'm happy to be here, and I hope I do well today!

Korea has an excellent transportation system. In big cities like Seoul, most people take the subway or the bus. The subway is fast, clean, and cheap, and you can get almost anywhere with it. For long distances, there's the KTX, our high-speed train. It can take you from Seoul to Busan in about two and a half hours. Taxis are also everywhere, and you can call one with an app. Where I live, it's a little different. It's a small city by the sea, so most people drive, and we use bridges and tunnels to get to other cities. One thing I love is the T-money card: you tap it once, and it works on buses, subways, and even taxis. Honestly, getting around Korea is really convenient.

I mostly drive. I live in a small city, and public transportation isn't as convenient here as in a big city. I drive to work every day, and it takes about 25 minutes. I like driving, because I can listen to my music and sip my coffee on the way. I basically turn my car into my own little cafe! When I go to Seoul or other big cities, though, I take the KTX, since driving there is a nightmare with all the traffic and parking. I also take the bus sometimes, especially when I want to have a few drinks. Overall, I prefer the freedom of having my own car. I can go wherever I want, whenever I want.

Yes, I have. The most common problem is crowding. During rush hour, the bus is packed like a can of sardines. You can hardly move, and sometimes you get stuck in the corner. But the most embarrassing experience was when I fell asleep on a bus. It was after a company dinner, and I'd had a few drinks. I was so tired that I dozed off. When I woke up, the bus was parked at the last stop, and the driver was staring at me! I had no idea where I was. It was almost midnight, and there were no more buses. I had to take a taxi all the way home, and it cost me a fortune. I just shook my head at myself. Since then, I always set an alarm on my phone when I take the bus late at night. Lesson learned!

My favorite place to go camping is a campsite in Namhae, which is a short drive from my city. It's next to a small valley, so you can hear the water running all night. The campsite is surrounded by tall pine trees, and the air is so fresh. It has a flat, grassy area for tents, a clean bathroom, and a small shop where you can buy firewood and ice cream. At night, the sky is full of stars. You can see them so clearly because there's no city light. There's also a short walking trail that leads up to a lookout point, with a view of the sea. I like it because it's quiet, and it's the perfect spot to unplug from work. I always make a pot of coffee in the morning, and it tastes ten times better outdoors.

I went camping for the first time about five years ago. I got interested in it by watching camping videos on YouTube. I'm always on my computer, so I'd watch people sitting by a campfire, cooking food, and drinking coffee in the middle of the woods. I thought, "That looks so relaxing." One day, I told a friend, "Let's try it!" She wasn't so sure at first, because she's not an outdoor person. We borrowed a tent from a friend, and we went to a campsite for one night. It was a bit of a disaster: we couldn't set up the tent, and the mosquitoes were terrible. But we loved the campfire, and we were hooked. After that, we bought our own gear.

My most memorable camping trip was to the campsite in Namhae, with a few friends. We drove there on a Friday evening, and it was already getting dark when we arrived. When I opened the trunk to set up the tent, I realized something terrible: I'd forgotten the tent poles! I had left them at home, in the garage. My friends just stared at me. I felt so embarrassed, especially because I'm the one who's always planning everything. But we didn't give up. I used the car's headlights to look around, and I found some long branches. One of my friends, who's very careful and smart, came up with a plan: we tied the tent to the car and to two trees. It looked ridiculous, but it worked! We grilled meat, roasted marshmallows, and looked at the stars. It was the best camping trip we've ever had. We still laugh about it, and now I have a checklist on my phone.

People in Korea spend their free time in lots of different ways. Hiking is really popular, especially among older people. On weekends, the mountains are packed with people in colorful hiking gear. A lot of people also go to cafes, because there's a cafe on every corner. Many people watch Netflix or YouTube at home, and younger people love playing games at a PC cafe with their friends. We also love singing at "noraebang", which is a karaoke room. And of course, people love eating out. Lately, camping and golf have become popular, too. I'd say Koreans work hard, but they know how to have fun.

My free time has changed a lot over the years. When I was a kid, I spent most of my free time outside. I played in the yard and ran around the neighborhood with my friends. With so many cousins and friends around, there was always something going on, like board games or dancing in the living room. When I was a student, I spent a lot of time at PC cafes, playing games with my friends. Now, I'm an adult with a busy job, so my free time is limited. These days, I like to relax at home: I listen to music, play computer games, or read. And on some weekends, I go camping with friends. I guess I've gone from "playing outside" to "playing it safe."

The last time I had free time was last Sunday. It was a really busy week at work, so I was looking forward to the weekend. I woke up late, around nine, and made a big cup of coffee. I sat by the window and read a book for about an hour. It was a novel I've been reading for weeks. After that, a friend and I went to a nearby beach for a short walk. The weather was perfect, sunny with a cool breeze. We picked up two iced americanos, sat on a bench, and watched the waves. In the evening, I played a few computer games, and we had dinner at home. It wasn't anything special, but it was exactly what I needed. I felt completely recharged.

Hello, I'm interested in booking a trip to Jeju Island with my friends. There will be three of us: two friends and me. First, do you have any package deals for three nights and four days?. Great. And what does the package include? Does it include the flights and the hotel?. I see. How much does it cost per person? Is there a discount for groups?. One last question: can I choose my own flight times? And do you offer a rental car?. That sounds perfect. Thank you so much for your help!

Hello, I made a reservation for a trip to Jeju with your agency, and I need to change my flight. I have a bit of a problem. Something came up: my company is holding a big team dinner on the day we planned to leave, and everyone has to attend. I feel terrible about changing the plan. Could you help me find another option? First, is there a later flight on the same day, maybe in the evening? If not, could we leave the next morning instead? Or, as a last option, could we move the whole trip to the following weekend? Any of those would work for me. Also, will there be any change fee? I'd really appreciate your help. Thank you!

Yes, I have, and it was a real scare. A few years ago, a friend and I planned a trip abroad. We had booked the flights and the hotel, and we were so excited. About two weeks before the trip, I was checking my documents, and I noticed something terrible: my passport was about to expire. Many countries require at least six months of validity, and mine had only three months left! I panicked. The next day, I took a day off work, and went to the city hall to apply for a new passport. Usually, it takes about a week, but I explained my situation, and they helped me out. I got the new passport just two days before the flight. Phew! Since then, I always check the expiration date on my passport first when I plan a trip. Even an IT guy can forget the basics!

Movies have changed a lot. When I was a kid, I watched movies on a small TV, usually on video tapes that my parents rented. We'd all squeeze together on the floor, eating snacks. Going to the movie theater was a special treat, because it only happened once or twice a year. Now, I can watch almost any movie at home, on a big screen, with Netflix or other streaming apps. The special effects are also much better. They look so real, and there's even 4D and IMAX. But some things haven't changed. A good story is still the heart of a movie. And I still love eating popcorn while watching one. The biggest difference, I think, is the "experience." We used to wait for a movie to come out. Now we can watch it anytime, which is convenient, but a little less special.

These days, my friends and I talk a lot about two things. The first one is the price of movie tickets. They've gone up so much, and it's expensive for a group of friends. We often say, "Why pay so much when we can wait for Netflix?" That's actually a big issue, because many people feel the same way, and movie theaters are struggling. The second thing is streaming versus theaters. Some people say that theaters will disappear. I don't think so, because there's nothing like a big screen. We also talk about Korean movies and dramas, because they're so popular around the world. It makes me proud. Every time a new movie comes out, my friends and I argue about which one to watch, but we usually end up compromising.
